parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two services are on the same broad topic, stock operations, but they don't share a consistent abstraction. ReceivingService loads data through the table gateways (ItemTable, BinTable), turns the rows into domain objects (Item, Bin) and lets those objects enforce the rules: bin.put, bin.take and item.needsReorder. It also checks for unknown bins and items in one place, its private item() and bin() helpers, and raises StockError. CycleCountService skips that design. It takes the raw PrismaService client and calls prisma.stockCount.create/findMany directly. It never uses the Bin domain object or BinTable, so a count can be recorded for a bin code that doesn't exist, which ReceivingService.bin() would have rejected. It also works out stock discrepancies from raw numbers outside the domain model. Inside CycleCountService, the discrepancy rule (counted vs expected, delta = counted - expected) is written out twice, in count() and openDiscrepancies(), instead of living in one place. So the module uses its own abstractions inconsistently and repeats a rule, which fails the rubric.

violations.message: Skips the module's data-access and domain abstractions: it injects PrismaService and calls prisma.stockCount directly, while ReceivingService works through ItemTable/BinTable and the Bin/Item domain objects. Bin codes are never validated against BinTable or Bin, so the unknown-bin rule that ReceivingService enforces with StockError is not applied here.
The discrepancy rule (counted !== expected, delta = counted - expected) is written out separately in count() and openDiscrepancies() instead of being kept in one place.
